title: A homogeneous independent local generating family remains independent after killing one variable
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a Noetherian commutative local $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], with maximal ideal $m$. Assume every residue class modulo $m$ is represented by an element of $k$. For $n\geq0$ let $x: \{0,\ldots,n\}\to A$ generate $m$. Suppose for every $r\geq0$ and homogeneous polynomial $f\in k[X_0,\ldots,X_n]$ of degree $r$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $f(x)\in m^{r+1}$ implies $f=0$. Then $x_0$ is a nonzerodivisor. If $q:A\to A/(x_0)$ is the quotient map, then for every degree-$r$ homogeneous polynomial $f\in k[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$, $f(q(x_1),\ldots,q(x_n))\in (q(m))^{r+1}$ implies $f=0$.

source.place: Proof steps 1–4: the expanded local dimension argument from lem-wf-same-lie-closed-subgroup, clause (2)

proof.text: Using the finite generating family, expand any b∈m as Σ a_i x_i. Choose c_i∈k with a_i-C(c_i)∈m. Then b-ΣC(c_i)x_i∈m². Degree zero representatives follow from residue surjectivity. Induct on d using product-ideal induction on m^(d+1)=m^d m: approximate each factor by a degree-d form and a degree-one form. The error terms lie in m^(d+2). Addition preserves the representatives. Thus every a∈m^d has a homogeneous representative g of degree d with a-g(x)∈m^(d+1).

If a∈m^d but a∉m^(d+1), its representative g is nonzero. If x_0 a∈m^(d+2), subtract x_0(a-g(x))∈m^(d+2). Independence gives X_0 g=0, contradicting that the polynomial ring over a field is a domain. Thus multiplication by x_0 raises finite order by exactly one.

If x_0 a∈m^(r+1) but a∉m^r, choose its last membership degree d using Ideal.exists_mem_pow_notMem_pow_succ_of_notMem_iInf. Then d<r, contradicting the preceding order calculation. Hence x_0 a∈m^(r+1) implies a∈m^r. Krull intersection gives intersection m^r=0. If x_0 a=0, strictness puts a in every power, so a=0. The local specialization of the Jacobson-intersection lemma is Mathlib Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isLocalRing.

Rename a degree-r form in the remaining variables into a form F not involving X_0. Lift its quotient membership: F(x)-z=x_0 b with z∈m^(r+1). For r=0, both z and (x_0) lie in m, so original independence gives F=0. For r=d+1, F(x)-z∈m^(d+1), so strictness gives b∈m^d. Represent b by a degree-d form g. Then (F-X_0 g)(x)=z+x_0(b-g(x))∈m^(d+2); independence gives F-X_0 g=0. Substitute X_0=0 and X_(i+1)=X_i to obtain f=0. This includes n=0.

theorem homogeneous_independence_quotient
    {k A : Type*} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin (n + 1) → A)
    (hres : ∀ a : A, ∃ c : k, a - algebraMap k A c ∈ maximalIdeal A)
    (hgen : maximalIdeal A = Ideal.span (Set.range x))
    (hind : ∀ (r : ℕ) (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) k), f.IsHomogeneous r →
      aeval x f ∈ maximalIdeal A ^ (r + 1) → f = 0) :
    x 0 ∈ nonZeroDivisors A ∧
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k), f.IsHomogeneous r →
        aeval (fun i ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {x 0}) (x i.succ)) f ∈
          (Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {x 0})) (maximalIdeal A)) ^ (r + 1) →
        f = 0
